questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-4z=2 \\ 4x+y-5z=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2z=1 \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+2z \\ y=-3z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+2z \\ -3z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

{\begin{aligned} & 2x+8y=-6 \\  & -4x-16y=12 \\  & 6x+24y=-18.\end{aligned}

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & -6 \\ -4 & -16 & 12 \\ 6 & 24 & -18\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & -6 \\ -4 & -16 & 12 \\ 6 & 24 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -3 \\ -4 & -16 & 12 \\ 6 & 24 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & 24 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+4y=-3\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-4y-3 \\ y=y,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-1 \\ -2{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-5{x}_{3}=-4 \\  & {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=5{x}_{3}-4 \\ {x}_{2}=1-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}={x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5{x}_{3}-4 \\ 1-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+2z=2 \\  & y-z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x=0 \\  & y-z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=0 \\ y=z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+2y=5 \\  & -10x-10y=-25 \\  & 8x+8y=20.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 5 \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 5 \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{5}{2}-y \\ y=y,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$

$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=2 \\  & -3x-4y=3 \\  & 2x-4y=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system is consistent dependent
- The system has a unique solution
- The system is inconsistent
questions.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & -4 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & -4 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & 9 \\ 2 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=-5,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement III is true.

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y=-1 \\  & 3x+y=3 \\  & -2x+y=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system is consistent dependent
- The system has a unique solution
- The system is inconsistent

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 \\ -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 5 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=2,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement III is true.

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+4y=-1 \\  & 2x+8y=-2 \\  & -3x-12y=3\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system is inconsistent
- The system is consistent dependent
- The system has a unique solution
questions.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 8 & -2 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 8 & -2 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x,$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we can find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*. 

As a result, only statement II is true.

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-3y=6 \\  & -2x+y=-3 \\  & 4x-4y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system is consistent dependent
- The system is consistent independent
- The system has no solution
questions.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 6 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 6 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation we have $y=-1$ and substituting this into the first equation yields $x=1.$ So,  we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement II is true.

questions.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & -2x+7y=6 \\  & x+ky=-3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 7 & 6 \\ 1 & k & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 7 & 6 \\ 1 & k & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & -3 \\ -2 & 7 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & -3 \\ 0 & 2k+7 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+ky=-3 \\  & (2k+7)y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=-\frac{7}{2},$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$, and we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $x+ky=-3.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=-\frac{7}{2}.$

\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042553/assets/81b7626ac30b06c5eeb10be274dd93476a86dce5fe3053722d96e16b78d7f165.png)

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $z,$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $z$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1-5y \\ y=y \\ z=3,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1-5y \\ y \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Classifying a System as Consistent Dependent, Consistent Independent, or Inconsistent
canonical_examples.problem:
Given the system
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042553/assets/5f1aaf29a3dd8b7ea2c4f7104d532f7b56f32a23ccebbcfa0d1bfe86c772cc5f.png)
which of the following statements are true?

- The system is consistent dependent

- The system has no solution

- The system is consistent independent
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042553/assets/6171d242b0a3887802f629de79cb952d47711a581e88db2d9304a5db356dfb62.png)

Using Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -4 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042553/assets/80aff0fd62e3e1aeed17017c864d8d0b875b556ce1a29a89e6c61e632bf9c733.png)

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
2x -3y= 4
$$

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, only statement I is true.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Value of a Constant for Which a Given Linear System Is Consistent or Inconsistent
canonical_examples.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-2y=1, \\ 4x+ky=-3\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042553/assets/a115d3da691619918bf92d914acdfdd95088e9a141a82ca3fe3230fa7fbb8172.png)

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & k & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & k+4 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042553/assets/cfea36ae2b5cb5d8715480c1e0ee0b5ba06cf39d0c2032eb6e9b9078bf8c5bde.png)

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=-4,$ then the second equation is $0=-5,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=-4.$
